summary: AHDB's first 2026 harvest report finds 90% of surveyed farms below their own five-year average for winter wheat, the clearest measure yet of how broadly the drought hit rather than how deeply. Only 10% of the 60-farm survey sample beat their five-year average. Reported farm yields span 3.9 to 11.5 t/ha around a 6.8 t/ha mean.
title: Report shows wheat yields below average on 90% of farms
verbatim_quote: The high cost of the exceptionally hot and dry weather on arable crops is becoming clearer, with the first AHDB harvest report showing that 90% of surveyed farms are below their five-year average for winter wheat.

summary: GB winter barley was 95% cut by the week ending 26 July, in what AHDB calls the earliest harvest since its records began in 2006. summary: CLA president Gavin Lane puts the physical damage in terms no yield figure carries: wheat at half its usual height and some crops not worth harvesting, after a sodden winter followed by drought. He notes this is the third drought in five years and calls it the new normal for British farming rather than an outlier.
title: Report shows wheat yields below average on 90% of farms
verbatim_quote: Farmers are telling us this is the worst harvest in years. A sodden winter followed by drought has left wheat at half its usual height and some crops not worth harvesting.

summary: POSITIVE, and the one thing the drought improved: GB wheat quality is exceptional. Group 1 specific weights range 76 to 85 kg/hl and protein averages 13.5%, with samples above 14% described as not uncommon. Low-yield, high-concentration grain is the classic dry-season trade-off and it partly offsets the tonnage loss for milling growers.
title: Report shows wheat yields below average on 90% of farms
verbatim_quote: Specific weights have been exceptional so far this year. For Group 1 samples, specific weights have ranged from 76 kg/hl to 85 kg/hl.

summary: Ghana's cocoa belt faces more rain on a crop already damaged by it. The Ghana Meteorological Agency's weekly outlook has rain and thunderstorms across the middle belt and transition zone, with the strongest signal at Sunyani. COCOBOD's crop has already been hit by excessive rain, disease and weak pod development, with Western and Western North worst affected by low cherelle counts. Further heavy rain and cloud would raise black pod risk, block spraying and cut sunlight.
title: Cameroon Cocoa Output Falls 20% as Ghana Faces Heavy Rain Risk (6 August 2026)
verbatim_quote: The rainfall requires close monitoring because Ghana's crop has already been affected by excessive rain, disease and weak pod development.

summary: Côte d'Ivoire's problem this week is the opposite of drought and not quite flood: farmers say the developing main crop now needs more sunshine after cooler, cloudy conditions. Moisture is adequate but insolation is not, which slows pod development and ripening. Another spell of widespread cloud across the West African belt would compound it.
title: Cameroon Cocoa Output Falls 20% as Ghana Faces Heavy Rain Risk (6 August 2026)

summary: Nearly every major commodity grown in Uvalde County was hit by the mid-July flood: corn, small grains, milo, cotton, hay and multiple vegetable crops.
